choreo.doc: M2-BPR-01/02: battle choreography (docs/kb/tech/battle_presentation.md). BattleChoreo plays each resolved action as beats: approach (the actor travels), strike (the action's clip, or its procedural motion), contact (at strike start + contact_at x strike_sec: the target reacts, damage floats and hit VFX land), recover, return. A KO collapses ko.delay_sec after contact. All times are seconds at battle speed 1.0; distances are metres. travel: 'target' runs to stop_short_m in front of the target(s); 'step' steps step_m toward them; 'none' stays on the mark. lunge_m, lift_m, crouch_m and lean_deg shape the procedural strike on a stand-in with no clip.

reaction.doc: The target's reaction on the contact beat. damage: recoil_m away from the actor and tilt_deg back, out and back over sec; heal: a lift_m rise; miss: a sidestep of dodge_m. clip names the model clip tried first (the clip contract).

enter.doc: A fighter swapped or called in walks onto its mark from back_m behind it.

reduced_motion.doc: UiSettings reduced motion: shorter travel and leans, no tilt on reactions.

speeds.doc: UiSettings battle_speed values (accessibility.json) the sequencer accepts.

outro.doc: M2-BPR-05: after the last action's choreography. victory: the standing party plays the victory clip, or a stand-in hops `hops` times hop_m high over sec, each fighter stagger_sec after the last, after delay_sec. escape: the party walks back_m back off the field over sec. The result panel waits for it plus settle_sec.

camera.doc: M2-BPR-03: the battle camera director (docs/kb/tech/battle_presentation.md, Camera director). Every shot is framed off the battle axis (party to foes, from the camera's authored default) so the party stays screen-right and the foes screen-left: the line is never crossed and the camera never rolls. anchor 'actor' is the actor's mark, 'strike' its strike point, 'target' the targets' middle, 'default' the authored default. A placed shot sits back_m behind the anchor along the axis, side_m toward the default camera's side and up_m above it, and looks at the point look_at of the way from the actor's mark to the targets, raised look_up_m. A 'default' shot moves push of the way from the default toward the raised targets and turns look_at of the way to them. fov (degrees) is optional: none keeps the default's. Blends: in over blend_in_sec from the sequence start, to the contact shot over to_contact_sec ending on the contact, out over blend_out_sec ending exactly on the sequence end (held at least hold_contact_sec after the contact). A shot that would put a target outside safe_frame (fractions of the screen kept clear for the HUD, at the design aspect) or the actor's head at its strike point off screen falls back to the default. by_style: a party action's lead and contact shots per style ('' holds the lead); enemy: every enemy action.
